proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(p=\mu_1\), \(q=\mu_0\), and \(c=1-\alpha\), so that \(\tau=1+c\).  We first record an elementary sumset inequality.  If \(A=\{a_1<\cdots<a_r\}\) and \(-B=\{b_1<\cdots<b_s\}\) are nonempty subsets of the integers, then
\[
a_1+b_1<\cdots<a_r+b_1<a_r+b_2<\cdots<a_r+b_s
\]
are \(r+s-1\) distinct elements of \(A-B\).  Hence
\[
|A-B|\geq |A|+|B|-1. \tag{1}
\]
This is a direct ordering argument and uses no positivity of the marginal cells.

We next establish the deterministic bounds.  If \(k^*=1\), a shortest valid set is a singleton and therefore an interval, so \(I^*=1\).  If \(k^*=2\), \(\mathrm{thm{:}all\mbox{-}minimizers}\) supplies a threshold-feasible pair \((A,B)\in\mathcal F_\tau\) with \(|A-B|=2\).  By (1), \(|A|+|B|\leq3\).  Since two singleton sets have a one-point difference set, the size pattern is \((|A|,|B|)=(1,2)\) or \((2,1)\).  Thus \(A-B\) is a translate or a reflected translate of a two-point subset of \(X\), and
\[
\operatorname{span}(A-B)\leq L-1.
\]
Its consecutive hull has at most \(L\) elements.  That hull contains the threshold-feasible difference set \(A-B\), so it is valid by \(\mathrm{thm{:}all\mbox{-}minimizers}\).  Therefore
\[
k^*=2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad I^*\leq L. \tag{2}
\]
If \(k^*\geq3\), the full effect support \(E\) is a valid interval: the product table \(\gamma_{ij}=p_iq_j\) shows that \(\Gamma(p,q)\) is nonempty, every \(\gamma\in\Gamma(p,q)\) has total mass one, and hence \(h_\mu(E)=1\geq c\).  Consequently
\[
k^*\geq3\quad\Longrightarrow\quad I^*\leq2L-1. \tag{3}
\]
Equations (2)--(3) give
\[
\frac{I^*}{k^*}\leq
\begin{cases}
1,&k^*=1,\\
L/2,&k^*=2,\\
(2L-1)/3,&k^*\geq3,
\end{cases}
\]
and
\[
I^*-k^*\leq
\begin{cases}
0,&k^*=1,\\
L-2,&k^*=2,\\
2L-4,&k^*\geq3.
\end{cases} \tag{4}
\]
Because \(L\geq3\), one has \(L/2\leq(2L-1)/3\) and \(L-2\leq2L-4\).  This proves the asserted high-coverage multiplicative bound, in fact without using \(\alpha<1/2\), and proves the additive bound for every \(0<\alpha<1\).

Suppose now that \(1/2\leq\alpha<1\), equivalently \(0<c\leq1/2\).  Partition \(X\) into two nonempty consecutive blocks \(B_1,B_2\), each of cardinality at most \(\lceil L/2\rceil\).  Since \(q(B_1)+q(B_2)=1\), some block \(B\) satisfies
\[
q(B)\geq\frac12\geq c.
\]
With \(A=X\),
\[
p(A)+q(B)=1+q(B)\geq1+c=\tau,
\]
so \((X,B)\in\mathcal F_\tau\).  If \(B=\{r,r+1,\ldots,r+b-1\}\), direct subtraction of integer intervals gives
\[
X-B=\{-(r+b-1),-(r+b-2),\ldots,L-1-r\},
\qquad |X-B|=L+b-1.
\]
Thus \(X-B\) is a valid interval by \(\mathrm{thm{:}all\mbox{-}minimizers}\), and
\[
I^*\leq L+\lceil L/2\rceil-1. \tag{5}
\]
When \(k^*\geq3\), (5) and the parity identities
\[
2\lceil L/2\rceil-2=
\begin{cases}
L-2,&L\text{ even},\\
L-1,&L\text{ odd}
\end{cases}
<L
\]
imply
\[
\frac{I^*}{k^*}\leq\frac{L+\lceil L/2\rceil-1}{3}<\frac L2. \tag{6}
\]
For \(k^*=1\), \(I^*/k^*=1<L/2\); for \(k^*=2\), (2) gives \(I^*/k^*\leq L/2\).  This proves the low-coverage bound.

We now prove sharpness at high coverage.  Fix \(0<\alpha<1/2\) and
\[
0<\varepsilon<\min\{\alpha/2,1-2\alpha\}.
\]
Let \(p=q\) have endpoint mass \(M=(1-\varepsilon)/2\) and common interior mass \(\varepsilon/(L-2)\).  These marginals are strictly positive and normalized.  For \(A=B=\{0,L-1\}\),
\[
A-B=\{-L+1,0,L-1\},
\qquad p(A)+q(B)-1=1-2\varepsilon>1-\alpha=c.
\]
The Hall representation in \(\mathrm{thm{:}all\mbox{-}minimizers}\) therefore makes this three-effect set valid.

Let \(S\subseteq E\) have at most two elements.  It omits at least one of \(-L+1,0,L-1\).  If it omits zero, the diagonal coupling \(\gamma_{ij}=p_i\mathbf 1\{i=j\}\) belongs to \(\Gamma(p,q)\) and gives \(\gamma\{i-j\in S\}=0\).  If it omits \(-L+1\), assign mass \(M\) to the cell \((0,L-1)\); if it omits \(L-1\), assign mass \(M\) to \((L-1,0)\).  In either corner case, the residual row and column marginals are nonnegative and have common total \(1-M>0\), so the normalized product of the residual marginals completes the corner mass to a coupling in \(\Gamma(p,q)\).  The selected corner has an effect outside \(S\), whence
\[
h_\mu(S)\leq1-M=\frac{1+\varepsilon}{2}<1-\alpha=c.
\]
Thus no set of cardinality at most two is valid and \(k^*=3\).  Every proper consecutive subset of \(E\) omits at least one extreme effect.  The corresponding corner coupling again yields coverage at most \((1+\varepsilon)/2<c\).  Since \(E\) is valid, \(I^*=2L-1\).  Hence
\[
\frac{I^*}{k^*}=\frac{2L-1}{3},
\qquad I^*-k^*=2L-4. \tag{7}
\]

For sharpness at the elbow \(\alpha=1/2\), take \(p=q\) with mass \(1/2\) at each endpoint and zero elsewhere.  The pair \(A=\{0\}\), \(B=\{0,L-1\}\) has mass sum \(3/2=\tau\) and two-point difference set \(\{-L+1,0\}\), so \(k^*\leq2\).  By (1), any rectangle whose difference set is a singleton has singleton sides, and its mass sum is at most one, which is strictly below \(\tau=3/2\).  Hence \(k^*=2\).  For these marginals, every proper outcome interval has mass at most \(1/2\).  Therefore, whenever \(a+b\leq L\),
\[
Q_1(a)+Q_0(b)\leq1,
\]
and equality is attainable; thus \(B_{L-1}=1<\tau\).  By \(\mathrm{thm{:}general\mbox{-}frontier}\), no valid effect interval has at most \(L-1\) points.  The consecutive hull \(\{-L+1,\ldots,0\}\) of the valid two-point set has \(L\) points and is valid, so \(I^*=L\).

Finally let \(1/2<\alpha<1\) and choose \(0<\varepsilon<(2\alpha-1)/3\).  Give both marginals endpoint mass \(M=(1-\varepsilon)/2\) and common interior mass \(e=\varepsilon/(L-2)\).  Because \(\alpha<1\), the displayed restriction implies \(\varepsilon<1/3\), and hence \(M>e\).  The same pair \(A=\{0\}\), \(B=\{0,L-1\}\) satisfies
\[
p(A)+q(B)=3M=\frac{3(1-\varepsilon)}2>2-\alpha=\tau,
\]
so its two-point difference set is valid.  A singleton difference set again forces singleton sides by (1), while the sum of any two atom masses is at most \(2M=1-\varepsilon<1<\tau\); hence \(k^*=2\).  For \(1\leq w<L\), a consecutive outcome block contains at most one endpoint, and the endpoint block is optimal because \(M>e\).  Consequently
\[
Q_0(w)=Q_1(w)=M+(w-1)e.
\]
For \(a+b\leq L\), it follows that
\[
Q_1(a)+Q_0(b)\leq2M+(L-2)e=1,
\]
with equality when \(a+b=L\).  Hence \(B_{L-1}=1<\tau\), so \(\mathrm{thm{:}general\mbox{-}frontier}\) rules out every effect interval shorter than \(L\).  The valid two-point set has an \(L\)-point consecutive hull, proving \(I^*=L\).  Thus \(I^*/k^*=L/2\), and the perturbed marginals are strictly positive and symmetric.  The constructions concern the shared unrestricted-coupling fixed-marginal class only, which proves the stated, expressly limited comparison.

Write \(c=1-\alpha\) and \(\tau=1+c\).  We use the deterministic case bounds proved in \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\mbox{-}interval\mbox{-}price}\):
\[
k^*=1\Longrightarrow I^*=1,
\qquad
k^*=2\Longrightarrow I^*\leq L,
\qquad
k^*\geq3\Longrightarrow I^*\leq2L-1. \tag{1}
\]

First suppose \(0<\alpha<1/2\).  If \(k^*=1\), then \(I^*/k^*=1\) and \(I^*-k^*=0\).  If \(k^*=2\), (1) and \(L\geq3\) give
\[
\frac{I^*}{k^*}\leq\frac L2<\frac{2L-1}{3},
\qquad
I^*-k^*\leq L-2<2L-4. \tag{2}
\]
If \(k^*\geq3\), then
\[
\frac{I^*}{k^*}\leq\frac{2L-1}{k^*}\leq\frac{2L-1}{3},
\qquad
I^*-k^*\leq2L-1-k^*\leq2L-4. \tag{3}
\]
Equality in either chain in (3) holds if and only if \(k^*=3\) and \(I^*=2L-1\).  Together with (2), this proves equivalence of the first three high-coverage conditions.

By \(\mathrm{thm{:}general\mbox{-}frontier}\),
\[
k^*=3\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R_2<\tau\leq R_3, \tag{4}
\]
and, because the full interval \(E\) is valid,
\[
I^*=2L-1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad B_{2L-2}<\tau. \tag{5}
\]
The profiles \(Q_d(w)\) are nondecreasing in \(w\): enlarging any optimizing consecutive block of width \(w<L\) by one adjacent category inside \(X\) cannot decrease its nonnegative mass.  Under \(1\leq a,b\leq L\) and \(a+b\leq2L-1\), every profile sum is bounded by one of the two sums corresponding to \((a,b)=(L,L-1)\) or \((L-1,L)\).  Since
\[
Q_d(L)=1,
\qquad
Q_d(L-1)=\max\{1-\mu_{d,0},1-\mu_{d,L-1}\}
=1-\min\{\mu_{d,0},\mu_{d,L-1}\},
\]
the definition of \(B_{2L-2}\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
B_{2L-2}
&=\max\{1+Q_0(L-1),Q_1(L-1)+1\}\\
&=2-\min\{\mu_{1,0},\mu_{1,L-1},\mu_{0,0},\mu_{0,L-1}\}.
\end{aligned} \tag{6}
\]
Because \(\tau=2-\alpha\), equations (4)--(6) prove equivalence of all five high-coverage conditions.

We next characterize equality when \(1/2\leq\alpha<1\).  The proof of \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\mbox{-}interval\mbox{-}price}\) shows more than its weak inequality: if \(k^*=1\), then \(I^*/k^*=1<L/2\), and if \(k^*\geq3\), then
\[
\frac{I^*}{k^*}\leq\frac{L+\lceil L/2\rceil-1}{3}<\frac L2. \tag{7}
\]
Therefore equality \(I^*/k^*=L/2\) is possible only when \(k^*=2\).  In that case (1) gives \(I^*\leq L\), so equality holds exactly when \(I^*=L\).  Conversely, \(k^*=2\) and \(I^*=L\) plainly give the ratio \(L/2\).

The arbitrary-set part of \(\mathrm{thm{:}general\mbox{-}frontier}\) gives
\[
k^*=2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R_1<\tau\leq R_2. \tag{8}
\]
Conditional on \(k^*=2\), the consecutive-hull argument in (1) gives \(I^*\leq L\).  The interval part of \(\mathrm{thm{:}general\mbox{-}frontier}\) then gives
\[
I^*=L\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad B_{L-1}<\tau, \tag{9}
\]
because the right-hand inequality excludes every interval of size at most \(L-1\), while \(I^*\leq L\) supplies a valid interval of size at most \(L\).  Combining (8)--(9) proves the three-way low-coverage equivalence.  Since \(R_1,R_2\), and \(B_{L-1}\) are maxima over the finite families displayed in \(\mathrm{def{:}frontier\mbox{-}profiles}\), this is a computable necessary-and-sufficient characterization, including threshold equalities and zero marginal cells.

It remains to prove the asserted existence boundary for nonsymmetric high-coverage equality.  Necessity follows from (6): \(I^*=2L-1\) implies that all four endpoint masses exceed \(\alpha\).  In either arm their sum is at most one, so necessarily \(2\alpha<1\).  Conversely, fix \(0<\alpha<1/2\), choose
\[
0<\varepsilon<\min\{\alpha/4,(1-2\alpha)/4\},
\qquad M=\frac{1-\varepsilon}{2},
\qquad 0<\delta<M-\alpha,
\]
and define \(q=\mu_0\) and \(p=\mu_1\) by
\[
q_0=q_{L-1}=M,
\qquad
p_0=M+\delta,
\qquad
p_{L-1}=M-\delta,
\]
and
\[
p_i=q_i=\frac{\varepsilon}{L-2},
\qquad 1\leq i\leq L-2.
\]
The vectors are normalized and strictly positive, and \(p\neq q\).  All four endpoint masses exceed \(\alpha\), so (6) gives \(B_{2L-2}<\tau\).  With \(A=B=\{0,L-1\}\),
\[
p(A)+q(B)=2(1-\varepsilon)>2-\alpha=\tau,
\]
and \(|A-B|=3\), whence \(R_3\geq\tau\).

To verify the remaining strict inequality, the ordering argument used in \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\mbox{-}interval\mbox{-}price}\) gives \(|A-B|\geq|A|+|B|-1\).  Thus \(|A-B|\leq2\) implies \(|A|+|B|\leq3\).  The two largest atoms in each marginal are its endpoints: indeed, \(M-\delta>\alpha>\varepsilon/(L-2)\).  Hence every rectangle entering \(R_2\) has mass sum at most
\[
(M+\delta)+(1-\varepsilon)
<(2M-\alpha)+(1-\varepsilon)
=2-2\varepsilon-\alpha
<2-\alpha=\tau.
\]
Therefore \(R_2<\tau\), and the high-coverage equivalences imply \(k^*=3\) and \(I^*=2L-1\).  This proves sufficiency and the exact \(\alpha<1/2\) existence boundary.  The half--half boundary witness and the strictly positive perturbations for \(\alpha>1/2\) were constructed and verified in \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\mbox{-}interval\mbox{-}price}\), completing the low-coverage attainment claim.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \(L\geq3\), every \((\mu_0,\mu_1)\in\Delta_L^2\), and every \(0<\alpha<1\),
\[
\frac{I^*}{k^*}\leq
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{2L-1}{3},&0<\alpha<\dfrac12,\\[3pt]
\dfrac L2,&\dfrac12\leq\alpha<1,
\end{cases}
\qquad
I^*-k^*\leq2L-4.
\]
Both regime-specific multiplicative constants are sharp.  If \(0<\alpha<1/2\), then for every
\[
0<\varepsilon<\min\{\alpha/2,1-2\alpha\},
\]
the strictly positive symmetric marginals having mass \((1-\varepsilon)/2\) at each endpoint and mass \(\varepsilon/(L-2)\) at each interior category satisfy \(k^*=3\) and \(I^*=2L-1\); hence they also attain the additive constant \(2L-4\).  If \(\alpha=1/2\), the symmetric law placing mass \(1/2\) at each endpoint and zero elsewhere satisfies \(k^*=2\) and \(I^*=L\).  If \(1/2<\alpha<1\), the same conclusion holds for every strictly positive symmetric perturbation with endpoint masses \((1-\varepsilon)/2\), equal interior masses \(\varepsilon/(L-2)\), and \(0<\varepsilon<(2\alpha-1)/3\).  Thus, only on the shared fixed-marginal ordinal class with unrestricted potential-outcome coupling, the marginal-robust ordinal interval oracle studied by ZhangRichardson2025 can exceed the shortest arbitrary-set oracle by exactly the displayed regime-specific sharp factors.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The active directive replaces the coarse all-coverage ratio bound by the proved sharp phase transition: the constant is \((2L-1)/3\) above one-half target coverage and \(L/2\) at or below one-half target coverage, with explicit boundary and strictly positive witnesses.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix \(L\geq3\), \((\mu_0,\mu_1)\in\Delta_L^2\), and \(0<\alpha<1\).  If \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the following five conditions are equivalent:
\[
\frac{I^*}{k^*}=\frac{2L-1}{3};
\]
\[
I^*-k^*=2L-4;
\]
\[
k^*=3\quad\text{and}\quad I^*=2L-1;
\]
\[
R_2<\tau\leq R_3\quad\text{and}\quad B_{2L-2}<\tau;
\]
and
\[
R_2<\tau\leq R_3
\quad\text{and}\quad
\min\{\mu_{1,0},\mu_{1,L-1},\mu_{0,0},\mu_{0,L-1}\}>\alpha.
\]
If \(1/2\leq\alpha<1\), the following three conditions are equivalent:
\[
\frac{I^*}{k^*}=\frac L2;
\]
\[
k^*=2\quad\text{and}\quad I^*=L;
\]
and
\[
R_1<\tau\leq R_2\quad\text{and}\quad B_{L-1}<\tau.
\]
The high-coverage equality system \(k^*=3\), \(I^*=2L-1\) has strictly positive nonsymmetric marginal solutions exactly when \(0<\alpha<1/2\).  The low-coverage equality system is attained at \(\alpha=1/2\) by the symmetric two-endpoint half--half law and, for every \(1/2<\alpha<1\), by strictly positive symmetric perturbations of that law.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The former statement characterized equality only for the coarse high-coverage constant. The replacement retains that characterization on \(\alpha<1/2\) and adds the exact, separately proved low-coverage equality system \(R_1<\tau\leq R_2\) and \(B_{L-1}<\tau\).

prose_updates.tldr: Randomization identifies the two ordinal potential-outcome marginals but not their coupling. The note characterizes every shortest coupling-robust individual-effect set as a high-mass difference set, gives an exact boundary-safe ternary disconnectedness frontier, and finds a sharp missed elbow in the price of interval reporting: the worst multiplicative price is \((2L-1)/3\) when target coverage exceeds one half and \(L/2\) when target coverage is at most one half. Exact min-cut computation and simultaneous multinomial confidence-polytopes provide finite-sample certification and uniform selector recovery away from explicit tie surfaces.

project_justification.gap: The closest ITE papers give sharp distributional bounds and marginal-robust interval-valued reports, but no located result solves the outer cardinality optimization over arbitrary ordinal effect sets or identifies the coverage-level elbow in the sharp interval price. Hall theory certifies a fixed support but does not solve that selection problem.
project_justification.niche: Ordinal outcomes create integer difference geometry in which disconnected sets can be dramatically shorter under every cross-world coupling, with the maximal interval penalty changing exactly when target coverage crosses one half.
project_justification.fill: The difference-set normal form, complete ternary frontier, sharp two-regime general-support interval price with matching equality systems, and confidence-polytope inversion jointly deliver identification, geometry, computation, and honest reporting.

prose_updates.related_work: Zhang and Richardson (2025), Sections 3 and 5, study marginal-robust ordinal ITE prediction intervals; Appendix D and their Theorem 12 establish sharp ordinal individual-effect probability-mass bounds. On the shared fixed-marginal class with unrestricted potential-outcome coupling, the present result enlarges their interval oracle to arbitrary effect sets and proves a sharp coverage-level elbow in the resulting interval price, without attributing an explicit open problem to that paper. Fan and Park (2010) are the direct sharp distribution-of-ITE comparator: they derive Makarov-type distribution-function bounds and inference, whereas the present target selects a shortest common-coupling set of effect values and characterizes when that set is disconnected. Koperberg (2024) supplies finite Strassen--Hall deficiency for a fixed relation and is used only as identification machinery. Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018) derive sharp scalar ordinal benefit bounds through cumulative transportation arguments; the present target is a common-coupling multi-diagonal set. Gao, Shan, Srinivas, and Vijayaraghavan (2025) motivate measuring the price of geometric restrictions, but their structured conformal sets are evaluated under an observed outcome law rather than an adversarial potential-outcome coupling. Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (2021) motivate simplex confidence-region inversion, Huang, Fang, Hanley, and Rosenblum (2019) address nonregular scalar ordinal-bound inference, and Fang and Santos (2019) explain why active-set ties require directional methods. Duarte and coauthors (2024) motivate exhaustive discrete computation but do not replace the symbolic frontier. Goldman and coauthors (2020) supply the seven-category randomized endpoint for the concrete application.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The Hall identity is established prior machinery specialized to this problem. The contribution is the optimizer-wide difference-set geometry, exhaustive ternary frontier, and the proved sharp interval-price phase transition with computable equality regimes. The extremal marginal laws certify worst-case constants and are not asserted to equal the empirical law in the remdesivir trial. The confidence result is finite-sample honest but makes no efficiency claim. Selector recovery is asserted only on \(\mathcal M_{L,\eta}\); exact recovery on tie surfaces is not claimed. When \(L=2\), the reduction agrees with Zhang and Richardson's result that the sole disconnected candidate cannot be shortest, providing the binary sanity check.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem quantifies exactly how much connected reporting can conceal and shows that the sharp penalty has an elbow at one-half target coverage.
statement_notes.gap: ZhangRichardson2025 studies the marginal-robust ordinal interval oracle on the shared fixed-marginal unrestricted-coupling class, while GaoShanSrinivasVijayaraghavan2025 compares structured sets under an observed response law; neither derives this sharp adversarial-coupling phase transition.
statement_notes.consumer: For the seven-category remdesivir endpoint, the sharp worst-case ratio is \(13/3\) above one-half target coverage and \(7/2\) at or below one-half target coverage; the constants describe the oracle class, not the observed trial law.

statement_notes.justification: The finite profile inequalities identify exactly when either branch of the sharp interval-price frontier is attained, including zero cells and threshold equality.
statement_notes.gap: A sharp factor without its equality regime would not reveal whether the coverage elbow is structural or merely an artifact of two examples; the profile characterization resolves that distinction.
statement_notes.consumer: The conditions can be evaluated from the identified arm marginals through \(R_1,R_2,R_3,B_{L-1}\), and \(B_{2L-2}\), while preserving the distinction between an oracle extremum and a claim about the remdesivir data.
